modv0.1.2

watchWait with no model running.

The mod watches a usage ceiling or runs a check command on a timer, stays silent, and tells the session once, when it should.

At the prompt of a terminal session:

/plugin install watch --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills
Other ways to install

  • From a shell:

    claude plugin install watch --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills

  • In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box, then Plugins, Add marketplace with LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills, then Add plugin.

Read automating-repetition Source on GitHub

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/watch usage 42 finish the release, then pausetell the session once at 42% of the weekly window
/watch usage 80 5hthe same for the 5-hour window
/watch every 5m curl -sf https://example.com/uprun it now and every 5 minutes, wake once when it exits 0
/watch every 1m --for 6h --note "install it" adb get-state
/watch testsend one real wake
/watch stop 2stop one watch; stop alone stops them all
/watchlist what is being watched

Who can start one

The model can start a usage ceiling itself, with the mcp__watch__usage_ceiling tool, rather than checking usage or dispatching an agent to check it. It cannot start a command watch. A check is a shell command run on a timer outside the permission system, so only a person typing /watch can start one. To wait on a command, the model has its own permissioned tools.

Only you can change a watch: /watch starts, stops or tests one only when you type it (at the terminal, in an app, or through Remote Control). A scheduled prompt, another plugin or another session running /watch gets the list and nothing else.

How it behaves

  • Usage. The mod reads what the host pushes when a window moves a whole point, so nothing polls. During a running turn the news arrives with the next tool result, and in an idle session as a new turn. Readings come from this session's own responses, so an idle session may not see usage spent elsewhere until its next reply. Off a subscription there are no windows, and some plans have no 5-hour window. If there is no reading, the mod says so when you start the watch, and that watch may never fire. A ceiling already passed starts nothing and says so. A usage watch ends after two weeks, checked hourly, so it ends even when no reading ever comes.
  • Commands run with sh -c in the session's folder, as you, once at the start and then on the timer. A check gets two minutes. A failing check is silent, and only an exit of 0 wakes the session. A command that cannot run (exit 126 or 127), or that times out three times running, stops the watch and says so. A command watch ends after 24 hours unless --for says otherwise, and says so when it gives up. Its output reaches the model labelled as output, not instructions.
  • /watch test proves a wake can reach this session. It says nothing about whether a command can run or a window is reported.
  • Watches last as long as the session, at most 8 at a time. Closing the session ends them. Other harnesses ignore this mod.
